stories.title: Provide private external integration configuration
stories.user_story: As the product owner, I want the slice's private service configuration available locally, so that squads can build and verify real integrations without committing secrets.
stories.why_now: The newly created .env.local must be validated without exposing values before credential-dependent engineering can begin safely.
in_scope: Create an ignored .env.local containing owner-supplied Telegram, OpenAI, and Google OAuth values plus locally generated token-encryption and dashboard-auth secrets and the fixed slice configuration.
Leave the Docker-generated local Supabase URL and server credential for S01-01, which owns starting the local stack.
Record only key names, configuration categories, and pass/fail results in evidence.
out_of_scope: Committing, logging, printing, or copying secret values into evidence.
Changing application source code.
Mutating Railway, Google, Telegram, Supabase, or OpenAI resources during Phase 1.

acceptance_criteria.given: The owner-supplied, locally generated, and fixed keys listed in .env.example, excluding the Docker-generated local Supabase pair
acceptance_criteria.then: every required pre-Supabase key is present, non-placeholder, and non-empty.

acceptance_criteria.given: .env.local exists
acceptance_criteria.when: repository ignore and status rules are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: the file and its values are not tracked by Git.

commands: node --env-file=.env.local -e 'const required=["TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN","TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET","TELEGRAM_OWNER_USER_ID","OPENAI_API_KEY","OPENAI_MODEL","OPENAI_PROMPT_VERSION","GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID","GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET","GOOGLE_OWNER_EMAIL","GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY","GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEY_VERSION","DASHBOARD_PASSWORD_HASH","DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET","OWNER_TIME_ZONE","PUBLIC_APP_BASE_URL"]; const missing=required.filter((key)=>{const value=process.env[key]?.trim(); return !value || /^<.*>$/.test(value)}); console.log(missing.length ? `Missing keys: ${missing.join(", ")}` : `Present keys: ${required.join(", ")}`); process.exitCode=missing.length ? 1 : 0'
verification.done_when: A reviewer sees a value-free pass result for every pre-Supabase configuration key and confirms that .env.local is ignored.

squad.rationale: Only the product owner should provide and validate private account credentials; engineering squads must not manufacture or copy them.

stories.title: Open the owner-only live dashboard
stories.user_story: As the configured owner, I want to authenticate and see Shiori's live empty state, so that I know the protected browser, API, and durable source of truth are connected.
stories.why_now: This is the thinnest end-to-end walking skeleton and establishes the owner, configuration, persistence, and browser seams used by every later story.
in_scope: Validate server configuration without exposing values and keep the value-free .env.example current.
Verify the configured owner password with Argon2id, issue a short-lived signed secure cookie, and rate-limit login attempts.
Protect all initial dashboard reads and refuse unauthenticated access without owner data.
Exclude .env.local and other local environment files from Git and container build contexts while retaining .env.example.
Read an empty live dashboard summary from Supabase/Postgres through Fastify.
Render login, loading, empty, and error states with manual refresh in the existing React application.
Preserve the public health endpoint and one-service production build.
Initialize the local Supabase project and migrations, use its Docker-generated URL and server credential in the ignored .env.local, and make it the repeatable owner-read verification environment.
out_of_scope: Telegram ingress or commitment creation.
Google OAuth or Calendar access.
Runtime sample commitments, summaries, outcomes, or history.
Dashboard commitment mutations or polished populated-state history.

acceptance_criteria.given: no valid owner session
acceptance_criteria.when: a dashboard page or owner API is requested
acceptance_criteria.then: owner state is refused and no protected data is exposed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured password and invalid-password attempts
acceptance_criteria.then: only the valid owner is admitted, a short-lived HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookie is issued, and repeated failures are rate-limited.

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated owner and an empty live database
acceptance_criteria.then: Fastify returns factual zero counts and no commitment records from Postgres.

acceptance_criteria.given: login, loading, empty, and API-failure conditions
acceptance_criteria.when: the browser is used at phone and desktop widths
acceptance_criteria.then: each state is explicit, usable, and contains no runtime mock product data.

acceptance_criteria.given: the dashboard is authenticated
acceptance_criteria.then: the visible last-updated time changes from a fresh owner API response.

acceptance_criteria.given: the new authentication and persistence boundaries
acceptance_criteria.when: the public health endpoint and production build are checked
acceptance_criteria.then: the existing health contract remains operational and the browser still ships from Fastify.

acceptance_criteria.given: the browser bundle, network calls, Git status, and container build context
acceptance_criteria.then: the browser contains no Supabase credential, accesses product data only through Fastify, and no local environment file is tracked or uploaded.

verification.done_when: From a clean checkout with the configured test database, a reviewer can log in, receive a live empty summary, refresh it, and confirm unauthenticated refusal on phone and desktop.

squad.rationale: The walking skeleton crosses the owner contract, browser states, security boundary, Fastify API, and live persistence, so product, design, implementation, and independent verification must stay aligned.

stories.title: Refuse unsafe Telegram ingress and answer status
stories.user_story: As the configured Telegram owner, I want only my private authenticated updates accepted and a safe status response, so that Shiori exposes no owner state to other chats.
stories.why_now: The owner and persistence seams now exist; this adds the smallest replay-safe Telegram vertical before any language-model or commitment mutation.
in_scope: Add POST /api/telegram/webhook with Telegram secret-header validation.
Accept only the configured numeric owner in a private chat and durably capture the private chat ID.
Persist only Telegram update identity and processing state, never the complete webhook payload.
Make update processing idempotent.
Return an empty /status response for the authenticated owner.
Return a generic refusal for unauthorized users or non-private chats without owner data.
out_of_scope: Free-text classification, OpenAI calls, drafts, commitments, or callbacks.
Telegram groups, channels, files, images, or voice.
Scheduled delivery.

acceptance_criteria.given: a Telegram webhook request with an invalid or missing secret header
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is refused before any owner or product state is read or changed.

acceptance_criteria.given: an update from a non-owner or non-private chat
acceptance_criteria.then: a generic refusal is produced and no owner data is exposed.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured owner's private chat
acceptance_criteria.then: the chat ID needed for scheduled delivery is stored without retaining the full payload.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured owner sends /status with no active commitments
acceptance_criteria.then: Shiori returns a factual empty status response.

acceptance_criteria.given: the same Telegram update ID is delivered more than once
acceptance_criteria.then: it produces no repeated state transition or duplicate processing record.

acceptance_criteria.given: the stored Telegram update record and application logs
acceptance_criteria.then: they contain no complete webhook payload, message text, credential, or owner-state disclosure.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can replay owner, non-owner, group, and invalid-secret fixtures and observe one accepted owner update, generic refusals, an empty status, and no retained payload.

squad.rationale: The story introduces a security-sensitive external boundary and user-facing refusal/status copy, with replay and retention behavior requiring independent QA.

stories.title: Validate one bounded three-way decision
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want Shiori to distinguish a promise request, implied intention, and ordinary question safely, so that language judgment cannot authorize product changes.
stories.why_now: Telegram ingress is safe and replay-aware; this isolates the strict provider contract and semantic boundary before durable conversation state is introduced.
in_scope: Introduce a provider-neutral DecisionEngine with strict structured output and an OpenAI Responses API implementation.
Classify explicit commitments, implied intentions, and ordinary questions without giving the model authorization.
Generate the API JSON schema, TypeScript result type, and runtime structural validation from one source without a new runtime dependency.
Semantically validate definition of done, absolute Asia/Singapore target, simple-action mode, missing fields, class, and bounded next action.
Use a tool-free, stateless Responses request with strict JSON schema, configured model and prompt version, server-only credential, and bounded timeout.
Map refusal, timeout, incomplete, HTTP, JSON, schema, and semantic failures into bounded non-authorizing results.
Verify one sanitized real-provider smoke and exhaustive deterministic adapter fixtures without retaining raw input, output, trace, or chain-of-thought.
out_of_scope: Telegram conversational orchestration, persistence, drafts, corrections, permissions, or inline actions.
Commitment, session, event, scheduled-message, Calendar, or dashboard state.
Open-ended tool selection, provider-managed conversation state, chain-of-thought storage, or runtime decision mock data.

acceptance_criteria.given: representative explicit, implied, and ordinary Telegram turns
acceptance_criteria.when: the strict DecisionEngine result is validated
acceptance_criteria.then: each turn receives the correct class, extracted fields, missing fields, and bounded next action.

acceptance_criteria.given: the production OpenAI adapter
acceptance_criteria.then: it uses configured server credentials, model, and prompt version with strict text-format JSON schema, no tools, store false, and a bounded timeout.

acceptance_criteria.given: a structurally valid decision
acceptance_criteria.then: invalid time zones, targets, simple-action/work-session combinations, class/action combinations, and missing-field claims are rejected.

acceptance_criteria.given: a refused, timed-out, incomplete, HTTP-failed, non-JSON, schema-invalid, or semantically invalid provider result
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns only a bounded failure class and no authorized application action.

acceptance_criteria.given: deterministic fixtures and one benign synthetic real-provider request
acceptance_criteria.when: tests, logs, tracked files, and evidence are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: the three-way contract is proven without tools, product mutation, raw input or output, provider trace, credential, or chain-of-thought retention.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can inspect the single-source strict schema, exhaustively exercise three-way and failure fixtures, and run one sanitized real-provider smoke without any product mutation or retained provider material.

squad.rationale: This story isolates the security-sensitive provider contract so staff can implement one bounded interface while PM and QA independently prove it cannot authorize state changes.

stories.title: Classify turns against bounded draft context
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want Shiori to distinguish a clarification, correction, separate promise, and permission response against my current draft, so that deterministic application code can preserve or update it without guessing.
stories.why_now: S01-03b proved that the completed three-way result is non-authorizing but lacks the draft-relative signal required for safe permission and correction transitions.
in_scope: Replace the string-only DecisionEngine input with current owner text plus bounded structured conversation context containing phase and validated draft fields but no prior raw messages or transcript.

Add one strict non-authorizing turn-relation result that distinguishes no relation, new request, clarification continuation, correction, separate request, permission accepted, and permission declined.
Semantically validate every relation against input class, conversation phase, missing fields, and structured draft context.
Preserve the existing strict schema, stateless tool-free Responses request, timeout, refusal, failure, redaction, and non-mutation boundaries.
Verify correction, collision, permission, clarification, invalid-relation, and one sanitized real-provider context case without retaining provider material.
out_of_scope: Telegram orchestration, user-facing copy, commands, inline actions, persistence, drafts, commitments, sessions, events, scheduled messages, Calendar, or dashboard state.
Application authorization or mutation based only on the model relation.
Provider-managed conversation state, raw-message history, transcript, trace, chain of thought, or new runtime dependencies.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bounded conversation phase and validated current draft context
acceptance_criteria.when: DecisionEngine receives the current owner turn
acceptance_criteria.then: the strict result identifies the applicable draft-relative relation without receiving any prior raw message or transcript.

acceptance_criteria.given: correction, separate-request, clarification, permission-accepted, permission-declined, and unrelated fixtures
acceptance_criteria.when: the result passes structural and semantic validation
acceptance_criteria.then: each relation is accepted only for compatible class, phase, missing fields, and structured context combinations.

acceptance_criteria.given: a contradictory, unsupported, incomplete, refused, timed-out, or provider-failed relation result
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns a bounded non-authorizing failure and cannot authorize or perform any product transition.

acceptance_criteria.given: controlled fixtures and one benign synthetic provider request with bounded context
acceptance_criteria.when: tests, captured requests, logs, tracked files, and evidence are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: the new relation contract is proven with store false, no tools, no prior raw context, no product mutation, and no retained provider material.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can prove from bounded context fixtures and one sanitized provider request that correction, collision, clarification, and permission relations are strict, non-authorizing, and free of prior raw-message retention.

squad.rationale: This story makes one security-sensitive interface change, with PM freezing semantics and QA independently proving that the new signal remains bounded and non-authorizing.

stories.title: Collect one restart-safe simple-action draft
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want Shiori to ask permission or one clarification at a time and remember the structured draft, so that my intent survives a restart without becoming a commitment.
stories.why_now: S01-03a1 provides a bounded draft-relative relation without authorization; this story can integrate it with Telegram and durable draft state while still exposing no consequential action.
in_scope: Pass authorized owner text and bounded current draft context through the S01-03a1 DecisionEngine contract without retaining raw messages.
Ask for definition of done before target when both are missing, and ask exactly one concise question per turn.
Interpret and persist absolute targets in Asia/Singapore while rejecting ambiguous, past, invalid, or work-session-shaped decisions.
Ask permission before an implied intention can create a draft, retaining at most one validated non-actionable audit row that can correlate the immediately following agreement.
Answer ordinary questions without creating or changing draft, commitment, session, scheduled-message, Calendar, or dashboard state.
Persist at most one 24-hour restart-safe active draft, preserve it on collisions, and increment its version once for an accepted replay-safe correction.
Represent a complete collected draft with exact no-save copy and no Confirm, Cancel, or other inline action.
out_of_scope: Confirmation summary, inline Confirm or Cancel actions, commitment creation, reminder creation, or product events.
Reminder delivery, saved-commitment outcomes, Calendar access, work sessions, recurrence, or dashboard changes.
Prompt or schema expansion beyond the S01-03a1 DecisionEngine contract.

acceptance_criteria.given: an explicit simple-action request missing definition, target, or both
acceptance_criteria.when: the authorized conversation continues across an application restart
acceptance_criteria.then: Shiori asks one concise question at a time in definition-then-target order and restores the structured draft without creating consequential records.

acceptance_criteria.given: an implied intention and its immediately following owner response
acceptance_criteria.then: permission is requested first, at most a bounded non-actionable audit row exists before agreement, and only a validated agreement may begin a draft.

acceptance_criteria.given: an ordinary question with or without an active draft
acceptance_criteria.then: the bounded answer is sent without changing the current draft or any other product state.

acceptance_criteria.given: one active draft, a correction, a replay, or a second commitment request
acceptance_criteria.then: the draft is never silently overwritten, an accepted correction increments its version once, and replay does not increment it again.

acceptance_criteria.given: a complete, expired, refused, failed, or semantically invalid conversation decision
acceptance_criteria.then: complete state exposes no action, expiry is terminal, failures preserve current state, and only the approved safe response is sent.

acceptance_criteria.given: conversation persistence, logs, and evidence
acceptance_criteria.then: they contain no raw owner message, transcript, provider payload or trace, chain-of-thought, commitment, session, event, or scheduled message.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can exercise all three conversation classes across restart, permission, correction, replay, collision, and expiry while observing one bounded draft and zero consequential records or raw-message retention.

squad.rationale: This story isolates user-facing clarification and permission behavior with restart-safe persistence, requiring design-owned copy and independent mutation/retention verification.

stories.title: Confirm or cancel the current simple-action promise
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want to review and explicitly confirm or cancel the collected simple action, so that exactly the approved promise and reminder become durable.
stories.why_now: S01-03b establishes a validated versioned draft; this story can now expose actions only alongside their atomic, replay-safe transition.
scope_refs: Scope §Telegram behavior — Inline actions and Idempotency
in_scope: Render the complete simple-action summary with definition of done, absolute SGT target/reminder time, Calendar not checked, and the no-Calendar-write statement.
Attach opaque draft ID, version, and action references for Confirm and Cancel without product text or secrets.
Preserve an active draft on a second request and rerender the current summary without silently overwriting it.
Accept corrections by incrementing the draft version and making all earlier actions stale.
Return safe current, stale, expired, cancelled, confirmed, and malformed action results.
Atomically confirm exactly one active commitment, one pending simple reminder, and bounded append-only creation events while terminating the draft.
Cancel the draft without creating commitment, session, schedule, or reminder state.
out_of_scope: Reminder delivery or Done/cancel transitions on a saved commitment.
Calendar access, work sessions, recurrence, or saved-commitment editing.
Further decision-engine classification or provider prompt expansion.

acceptance_criteria.given: a current complete simple-action draft
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows definition of done, absolute SGT target/reminder time, Calendar not checked, the no-Calendar-write statement, Confirm, and Cancel.

acceptance_criteria.given: one active draft, a correction, or a second commitment request
acceptance_criteria.then: the draft is never silently overwritten, accepted corrections increment its version once, and the full current summary is shown.

acceptance_criteria.given: an old-version, malformed, expired, cancelled, or already-confirmed action
acceptance_criteria.when: it is received through the authorized Telegram boundary
acceptance_criteria.then: no consequential transition occurs and a safe stale or resolved response is returned.

acceptance_criteria.given: the current Confirm action
acceptance_criteria.then: one commitment, one pending simple reminder, and their bounded creation events are stored atomically and the draft becomes confirmed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a replayed or concurrent current Confirm action
acceptance_criteria.then: no duplicate commitment, reminder, event, acknowledgement, or follow-up message is produced.

acceptance_criteria.given: the current Cancel action
acceptance_criteria.then: the draft becomes cancelled and no commitment, session, schedule, reminder, or creation event is stored.

acceptance_criteria.given: a controlled database failure during Confirm
acceptance_criteria.then: no partial row is retained and the owner is not told the promise was saved.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can inspect a current complete draft, confirm or cancel it, replay every action class, and prove one all-or-nothing simple commitment and reminder transition.

squad.rationale: This half isolates the consequential user action, versioned callbacks, and multi-row transaction so implementer-independent QA can prove atomicity and replay safety.

open_questions: AC4 requires bounded append-only creation events, but scope and ADR explicitly name commitment.created without defining a reminder-creation event or exact event count. PM recommends exactly two uniquely keyed events in the Confirm transaction: commitment.created and scheduled_message.created. Owner approval is required before implementation.

stories.title: Deliver and resolve the simple reminder
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want my confirmed simple action reminded once and closable with Done, so that the promise is followed through without duplicate or nagging messages.
stories.why_now: A confirmed simple action and durable pending reminder now exist; this completes the first reminder/outcome loop before Calendar-aware sessions deepen it.
scope_refs: Scope §Telegram behavior — Inline actions and Idempotency
in_scope: Poll and transactionally claim due simple reminders from Postgres.
Send one Telegram reminder with Done and Cancel actions using a unique logical delivery key.
Record delivered, known retryable, or delivery-unknown results honestly.
Accept Done once, record the actual completion time, and cancel unsent messages atomically.
Return resolved state for a replayed Done action.
Create no follow-up after reminder non-response.
out_of_scope: Restart and concurrent-claim stress beyond the base transaction contract.
Saved-commitment cancellation semantics, which belong to S01-06.
Work-session start or end messages.
External queues, Redis, cron jobs, or additional replicas.

acceptance_criteria.given: one due simple reminder
acceptance_criteria.then: the message is transactionally claimed under its unique logical key and one attempt event is recorded.

acceptance_criteria.given: Telegram confirms the send
acceptance_criteria.then: one reminder with Done and Cancel is recorded as delivered.

acceptance_criteria.given: an active commitment and the reminder's current Done action
acceptance_criteria.then: the commitment closes once at the actual completion time and pending messages are cancelled atomically.

acceptance_criteria.given: a replayed Done action or repeated due-item observation
acceptance_criteria.then: no second completion, delivery, or ledger event is created.

acceptance_criteria.given: a known-safe failure or ambiguous send result
acceptance_criteria.then: known-safe retries are bounded and ambiguity becomes delivery_unknown without automatic resend.

acceptance_criteria.given: the owner does not respond
acceptance_criteria.when: the remaining schedule and ledger are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no additional notification exists and the commitment remains outstanding.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can advance a due reminder, observe one logical delivery, press Done once, replay it safely, and inspect that non-response schedules no follow-up.

squad.rationale: The first scheduled user-facing message joins delivery semantics, callback copy, transactional state, and outcome intent; QA must verify it independently of the implementer.

stories.title: Make scheduled delivery restart-safe
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want reminders to survive restarts without deliberate duplicates, so that scheduled follow-through remains durable and honest.
stories.why_now: The base scheduler works; reliability must be hardened before work-session start and end messages depend on it.
scope_refs: Scope §Rabbit holes and patches — Exactly-once Telegram delivery is impossible
Scope §Rabbit holes and patches — Deployment restarts lose timers
in_scope: Enforce unique logical delivery keys and concurrent transactional claims.
Recover expired claim leases after a bounded period.
Preserve pending schedules across process and Railway restarts.
Bound known-safe retries while keeping the same logical identity.
Record a definitive non-retryable provider rejection as terminal permanent_failure and never retry it.
Mark ambiguous sends delivery_unknown and never automatically resend them.
Verify claim and uniqueness constraints against a real disposable Postgres target.
out_of_scope: New user-facing reminder types.
More than one Railway replica.
External queues, Redis, cron jobs, or Supabase Edge Functions.
Changing the at-most-once bias accepted by the ADR.

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple workers poll the same due logical message
acceptance_criteria.when: the database claim function runs concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: only one current lease is granted and one logical attempt identity exists.

acceptance_criteria.given: a process stops after claiming but before a definitive result
acceptance_criteria.when: the bounded lease expires and the service resumes
acceptance_criteria.then: the claim is recovered only under the ADR's safe retry rules.

acceptance_criteria.given: a pending schedule before a Railway restart
acceptance_criteria.then: the durable item remains claimable without creating a duplicate schedule.

acceptance_criteria.given: a known-safe retryable failure
acceptance_criteria.then: attempts remain bounded and reuse the logical key.

acceptance_criteria.given: an ambiguous external send result
acceptance_criteria.then: the state is delivery_unknown and no automatic resend occurs.

acceptance_criteria.given: a definitive non-retryable provider rejection
acceptance_criteria.then: the state is terminal permanent_failure and no retry is scheduled.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can run concurrent claim, expired lease, restart, safe retry, permanent-rejection, and ambiguous-send scenarios and observe one durable logical schedule with no deliberate duplicate.

squad.rationale: This is a database-coordination and delivery-semantics hardening story with no new visual surface; PM guards the guarantee while staff and QA prove it under failure.

stories.title: Manage active promises through status
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want to review, complete, or cancel active promises from Telegram, so that I can manage the saved state explicitly without editing it.
stories.why_now: The simple reminder loop is durable; this completes the bounded Telegram management surface before work sessions and the rich dashboard rely on its terminal states.
scope_refs: Scope §Telegram behavior — Inline actions and Idempotency
in_scope: List active commitments by target with definition of done, target, overdue state, next simple reminder or work session, and Calendar-check status.
Expose only Done and Cancel actions from /status.
Allow Done once from /status or the reminder and record late completion time.
Cancel a draft directly.
Require a second explicit confirmation before cancelling a saved commitment.
Cancel unsent messages while preserving append-only events.
Reject stale or replayed management actions safely.
out_of_scope: Editing a saved commitment or moving its target.
Dashboard write controls.
Undo, reopen, recurring commitments, Snooze, or Skip.
Calendar writes.

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple active commitments
acceptance_criteria.then: they are ordered by target and show every scope-required status field with Done and Cancel only.

acceptance_criteria.given: an active or overdue commitment
acceptance_criteria.when: Done is accepted from /status or a reminder
acceptance_criteria.then: it closes once at the actual completion time and unsent messages are cancelled.

acceptance_criteria.given: a draft Cancel action
acceptance_criteria.then: the draft becomes cancelled and no commitment or reminder is created.

acceptance_criteria.given: an active saved commitment
acceptance_criteria.then: Shiori asks for a second explicit confirmation without changing the commitment.

acceptance_criteria.given: the second current cancellation confirmation
acceptance_criteria.then: the commitment closes once, unsent messages are cancelled, prior events remain append-only, and no Calendar write occurs.

acceptance_criteria.given: a stale, repeated, or already-resolved Done or Cancel action
acceptance_criteria.then: the current resolved state is returned without another transition or event.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can inspect an ordered /status response, complete once, cancel only after the second confirmation, and replay every action without changing counts.

squad.rationale: The story is a user-facing consequential-action flow whose copy, double confirmation, state transitions, and idempotency need all four roles.

stories.title: Connect the owner's read-only Calendar
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want to connect and reconnect my personal Google Calendar securely, so that Shiori can check availability without gaining write access.
stories.why_now: The protected dashboard and owner session exist, allowing the Calendar connection to be added independently before any availability behavior depends on it.
in_scope: Start Connect/Reconnect only from a valid owner session with OAuth state bound to that session.
Request offline access and the minimum identity plus read-only Calendar scopes.
Verify the returned Google identity exactly matches the configured owner email.
Exchange credentials server-side and expose no token or authorization code to browser JavaScript.
Authenticated-encrypt the refresh token before persistence and atomically replace it on Reconnect.
Represent disconnected, connected, authorization-expired, and temporarily unavailable states.
Use only the personal account's primary Calendar.
out_of_scope: Disconnect or revocation.
Google OAuth production verification or publishing.
Calendar writes, multiple accounts, multiple Calendars, or a full agenda.
Availability calculation or work-session confirmation.

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid owner session
acceptance_criteria.then: OAuth state is owner-session-bound and only required identity plus read-only Calendar scopes are requested.

acceptance_criteria.given: a callback with invalid state or a different Google email
acceptance_criteria.then: no connection or token is stored.

acceptance_criteria.given: a matching configured owner account
acceptance_criteria.then: the refresh token is authenticated-encrypted before durable storage and never exposed to the browser.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing connection
acceptance_criteria.then: the encrypted credential and metadata are replaced atomically.

acceptance_criteria.given: disconnected, connected, expired, and temporarily unavailable states
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows the exact state and the applicable Connect or Reconnect action.

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendar authorization expires or Google is unavailable
acceptance_criteria.then: they remain available and the health endpoint stays a liveness signal.

acceptance_criteria.given: the granted scopes, Calendar identifier, browser bundle, logs, and database
acceptance_criteria.then: only primary-Calendar read access exists and no plaintext token, code, credential, or browser-visible secret is present.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can connect and reconnect the matching test account through the protected dashboard and prove read-only primary-Calendar scope, encrypted storage, and no token exposure.

squad.rationale: The story adds a security-sensitive dashboard flow, cryptographic persistence, provider integration, and visible recovery states requiring full cross-functional ownership.

stories.title: Calculate deterministic work windows
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want Shiori's proposed work windows to obey my real Calendar constraints, so that every offered option is valid and explainable.
stories.why_now: The connected Calendar and durable draft contracts now exist; the deterministic scheduling boundary can be proven before any Confirm button exposes it.
scope_refs: Scope §Core concepts — Work session and Recovery session
in_scope: Create a bounded Calendar adapter for the primary Calendar and allowed event fields.
Use Google FreeBusy as the authority for blocked intervals.
Calculate candidates in Asia/Singapore for 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes.

Enforce default hours, explicit constraints, 30-minute boundaries, no midnight crossing, all-day busy, transparency, cancellation, a 14-day cap on generated pre-target searches, and a seven-day recovery cap.
Allow an exact owner-proposed interval beyond 14 days to be checked when it still begins no later than the immutable target.
Rank same-day later then earlier slots, then future slots, and return at most two alternatives.
Return no fit rather than relaxing constraints.
Keep event details out of model requests, durable product history, and unrestricted logs.
out_of_scope: Saving a work session or scheduling its messages.
User-facing confirmation, keep-conflict, or unverified-save flows.
Calendar writes, buffers, optimality claims, continuous monitoring, or multiple Calendars.

acceptance_criteria.given: a requested duration and Calendar busy intervals
acceptance_criteria.then: only 30, 60, 90, or 120 minute sessions in Asia/Singapore on 30-minute boundaries are considered.

acceptance_criteria.given: default hours, explicit constraints, midnight, all-day events, transparent events, and cancelled events
acceptance_criteria.then: every rule in the scope is applied deterministically without adding buffers.

acceptance_criteria.given: a generated target search, an explicit owner-proposed interval, or a recovery search
acceptance_criteria.then: generated pre-target search is capped at 14 days, an exact owner proposal beyond that cap may still be checked if it begins no later than the target, and recovery search is capped at seven days.

acceptance_criteria.given: a conflicting proposed time
acceptance_criteria.then: same-day nearest later then nearest earlier slots are preferred, followed by future chronological slots, with at most two results.

acceptance_criteria.given: no proposed time
acceptance_criteria.then: the earliest two fitting windows are returned without calling them objectively optimal.

acceptance_criteria.given: no window satisfies the policy
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is no-fit and no constraint is silently relaxed.

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendar adapter responses, model requests, persistence, and logs
acceptance_criteria.then: only allowed read-only fields enter the adapter and no Calendar event title or full object enters the model or product history.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can run fixed Calendar timelines through every availability and ranking rule and inspect that no event data crosses into the model or durable history.

squad.rationale: This is a deterministic policy engine with privacy boundaries and no new visual surface; PM owns the rule matrix while staff and QA implement and independently exhaust it.

stories.title: Confirm one Calendar-aware work session
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want to choose and explicitly confirm one realistic work session around Calendar constraints, so that my promise has one durable next action without changing Google Calendar.
stories.why_now: Decision, draft, availability, Google connection, and durable scheduler contracts are stable; this story joins them into the central Calendar-aware confirmation vertical.
scope_refs: Scope §Main user journeys — Explicit one-off commitment with work time
Scope §Calendar policy — Availability rules and Alternative ranking
Scope §Rabbit holes and patches — A Calendar suggestion becomes stale
in_scope: Offer work-time help only when work appears needed before the target and no window was supplied.
Collect one supported duration and owner timing constraints.
Present free windows or a sanitized conflict with at most two valid alternatives.
Require a new explicit confirmation to keep a conflicting time.
Bind suggestions and buttons to the current draft version.
Recheck Calendar availability at final confirmation and block a newly introduced conflict.
Offer and explicitly confirm an unverified save when Calendar is unavailable.
Atomically create one commitment, one future work session, one start reminder, one end check-in, and append-only events.
out_of_scope: Sending the start or end messages.
Continuation, recovery, or more than one future session.
Calendar writes or post-save conflict monitoring.
Automatic target movement or constraint relaxation.

acceptance_criteria.given: a possible duration-based commitment with no supplied work window
acceptance_criteria.then: Shiori offers help and collects one supported duration, while simple actions do not receive that offer.

acceptance_criteria.given: a free selected window
acceptance_criteria.then: definition of done, target, start/end, duration, check result/time, and the no-Calendar-write statement are explicit.

acceptance_criteria.given: a busy proposed window
acceptance_criteria.then: Shiori explains the conflict without unrelated event exposure and offers no more than two correctly ranked valid alternatives.

acceptance_criteria.given: the owner chooses to keep a conflict
acceptance_criteria.then: a new explicit confirmation is required and the saved session records conflict-kept.

acceptance_criteria.given: a previously free slot becomes busy before Confirm
acceptance_criteria.then: saving is blocked and new choices are produced.

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendar is unavailable at confirmation
acceptance_criteria.when: the owner explicitly confirms Save without Calendar check
acceptance_criteria.then: the session is saved as unverified and is never described as free.

acceptance_criteria.given: a current acceptable final check
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one commitment, one future session, one start item, one end item, and their events are created atomically, and replay creates no duplicate.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can exercise free, busy, kept-conflict, newly changed, and unavailable Calendar timelines and observe only the explicitly confirmed single work session and two durable messages.

squad.rationale: This is the slice's central user flow, joining deterministic Calendar policy, consequential copy and confirmation, atomic persistence, and scheduling under independent QA.

stories.title: Continue or recover after a work session
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want one start reminder, one end check-in, and an explicit option for one more attempt, so that Shiori records what happened without creating an open-ended plan.
stories.why_now: A single work session and durable message pair can now be confirmed; this completes its outcome, continuation, and recovery loop.
scope_refs: Scope §Main user journeys — Missed or incomplete work session
Scope §Rabbit holes and patches — Work-session continuation becomes an unbounded plan
in_scope: Deliver exactly one start reminder with Done and one end check-in with Done, Need more time, and Missed this session.
Suppress the end check-in when the commitment is already done or cancelled.
Record Done, partial work without a percentage, or missed work exactly once.
Ask for remaining duration after Need more time and whether another window is wanted after Missed.
Create no next session until the owner explicitly opts in, selects a Calendar-checked window, and confirms it.
Enforce at most one future planned session and preserve ordered past-session history.

After no pre-target slot fits, allow a recovery slot to be offered before the target passes, require it to start after the target within the seven-day recovery range, keep the target immutable, and derive overdue only after the target passes.
Create no additional notification after non-response.
out_of_scope: Automatic continuation, automatic recovery, multiple planned sessions, or target movement.
Progress percentages, coaching, behavioral inference, Snooze, or Skip.
Calendar writes or ongoing conflict monitoring.

acceptance_criteria.given: a due planned session
acceptance_criteria.then: one start reminder is delivered and, if the commitment remains active, one end check-in is delivered with the exact allowed actions.

acceptance_criteria.given: Done at the start, end, or /status
acceptance_criteria.then: the session and commitment close once and any unsent end or future messages are cancelled.

acceptance_criteria.given: Need more time
acceptance_criteria.then: partial work is recorded without a percentage, the commitment remains active, and Shiori asks for remaining duration without creating a future session.

acceptance_criteria.given: Missed this session
acceptance_criteria.then: no work is recorded, the commitment remains active, and Shiori asks whether another window is wanted without creating one automatically.

acceptance_criteria.given: the owner explicitly requests another attempt
acceptance_criteria.when: a version-current Calendar-checked window is confirmed
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one next session and its two messages are added while all past results remain append-only.

acceptance_criteria.given: no fitting pre-target window remains
acceptance_criteria.when: recovery is evaluated before or after the target and a recovery session is confirmed
acceptance_criteria.then: it may be offered immediately, begins after the target within the seven-day recovery range, leaves the target unchanged, and the commitment becomes or remains overdue only after the target passes.

acceptance_criteria.given: no response, restart, or replay of a start, end, or outcome action
acceptance_criteria.when: the schedule and ledger are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no additional notification, duplicate logical delivery, duplicate session, or duplicate outcome exists.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can drive start, end, Done, Need more time, Missed, decline, continuation, proactive recovery, non-response, and replay paths while observing at most one future session, an immutable target, and time-derived overdue state.

squad.rationale: The story completes a user-visible state machine across timed delivery, nuanced outcome copy, Calendar reuse, uniqueness constraints, and recovery semantics.

stories.title: Show the same live state on the dashboard
stories.user_story: As the owner, I want a clear read-only view of every live commitment, session, delivery, and outcome, so that I can trust Telegram and the dashboard show the same truth.
stories.why_now: All product states now exist in the single source of truth, so the initial dashboard skeleton can be deepened without inventing data or becoming a second management surface.
scope_refs: Scope §Rabbit holes and patches — Dashboard becomes a second management surface
in_scope: Derive active, due-today, and overdue counts in Asia/Singapore.
Show active cards with definition of done, target, next session or reminder, duration, historical Calendar status, and delivery state.
Show past work-session results, recent completed and cancelled commitments, and short append-only event history.
Show Google connection state, connected owner email, and last successful Calendar check.
Support factual populated, empty, loading, and error states.
Show last-updated time and manual refresh.
Provide usable phone and desktop layouts.
Expose no commitment creation, edit, completion, cancellation, or rescheduling API or control.
out_of_scope: WebSockets or live subscriptions.
Full Calendar agenda or Calendar mutation.
Commitment management from the dashboard.
Runtime sample data, weekly analytics, coaching, patterns, or experiments.

acceptance_criteria.given: live owner data
acceptance_criteria.then: active, due-today, and overdue counts are derived correctly in Asia/Singapore.

acceptance_criteria.given: active simple and duration-based commitments
acceptance_criteria.then: every required target, next action, duration, Calendar-check, and delivery field matches the source of truth.

acceptance_criteria.given: past sessions and terminal commitments
acceptance_criteria.then: session results, recent done/cancelled records, and append-only events are factual and ordered.

acceptance_criteria.given: each Google connection health state
acceptance_criteria.then: connection status, configured email, last successful check, and Connect/Reconnect affordance are accurate.

acceptance_criteria.given: populated, empty, loading, error, and manual-refresh conditions
acceptance_criteria.then: the corresponding explicit state and last-updated time are visible.

acceptance_criteria.given: phone and desktop widths
acceptance_criteria.then: authentication and every required factual field remain usable.

acceptance_criteria.given: the dashboard UI, API routes, browser bundle, and network calls
acceptance_criteria.then: all product data is live through Fastify and no commitment mutation or direct Supabase access exists.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can match representative entity IDs and timestamps across Telegram, ledger, owner API, and responsive dashboard, including empty/error states, with no dashboard mutation.

squad.rationale: This is the complete read-only visual product surface, requiring PM field coverage, designer state/layout ownership, staff read-model work, and independent API/browser parity verification.

stories.title: Verify and ship the deployed slice
stories.user_story: As the product owner, I want redacted deployed evidence for every accepted behavior and boundary, so that the slice can be declared shipped honestly.
stories.why_now: All implementation stories and automated gates are complete; the slice still requires real-service Railway verification and an indexed evidence record.
in_scope: Run the clean-checkout typecheck, API tests, production build, browser tests, and real database checks with Node 24.
Deploy the current source to the dedicated shiori-slice-01 Railway service, use one replica, and observe terminal deployment success without targeting or changing shiori-spike.

Use connected Railway tooling to resolve and record the explicit project, environment, service, and public domain, then run a value-redacting release command that refuses a dirty tree, records the exact HEAD SHA, deploys only that source state, and waits for terminal status.
Configure and verify the Telegram webhook and Google OAuth local/deployed callback without recording secrets.
Exercise evidence scenarios S1–S28 against the deployed service where safe and use controlled deterministic fault injection where production injection is not approved.
Verify restart, replay, authorization, Calendar scope, model privacy, persistence privacy, delivery ambiguity, and dashboard parity boundaries.
Store redacted artifacts under evidence/<story-id>/ and make the slice evidence.md the index.
Record environment, commit, deployment, model, prompt, migration, limitations, results, and final sign-off.
out_of_scope: New product behavior or weakened acceptance criteria.
Unapproved destructive production fault injection.
Formal evaluation platforms, repeated scoring, performance studies, cost studies, or trace-analysis systems.
Secrets, OAuth codes, tokens, cookies, authorization headers, unrelated Calendar events, or unrelated personal conversations in evidence.

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean checkout on Node 24 with approved configuration
acceptance_criteria.when: the full repository and database verification commands run
acceptance_criteria.then: typecheck, API tests, build, browser tests, and database constraints all pass.

acceptance_criteria.given: the source state selected for release
acceptance_criteria.then: the current deployment reaches terminal SUCCESS on one replica and the public health endpoint returns the agreed liveness response.

acceptance_criteria.given: the configured real Telegram, OpenAI, Supabase, and Google services
acceptance_criteria.then: the complete intention, simple-action, Calendar-aware, reminder, outcome, recovery, non-response, and cancellation journeys pass.

acceptance_criteria.given: restart, webhook replay, callback replay, unauthorized access, and ambiguous-delivery exercises
acceptance_criteria.when: evidence scenarios S19–S23 and S27 run
acceptance_criteria.then: durability, uniqueness, owner boundaries, and honest delivery state pass without duplicate product transitions.

acceptance_criteria.given: Calendar, model, persistence, logs, browser bundle, Telegram, ledger, API, and dashboard inspection
acceptance_criteria.when: evidence scenarios S24–S26 and S28 run
acceptance_criteria.then: read-only/allowed-field, privacy, retention, server-only data access, and live parity boundaries pass.

acceptance_criteria.given: all scenario artifacts
acceptance_criteria.then: it links redacted evidence for S1–S28, records known limitations and any owner-approved deviations, and contains no secret or unrelated personal data.

acceptance_criteria.given: any failed scenario or unapproved deviation
acceptance_criteria.then: the slice remains unshipped and the defect returns to its owning story without weakening an acceptance criterion.

verification.done_when: A reviewer can start from the recorded commit, observe a terminal-success Railway deployment, follow the evidence index through passing S1–S28 artifacts, and match the deployed health and dashboard parity without finding secrets.

squad.rationale: Shipping requires PM scope sign-off, designer review of deployed states, staff support for deployment and diagnostics, and QA ownership of independent S1–S28 evidence.
